areas_of_law: Public health emergency law / aviation and rail regulation
Civil procedure (mootness, discretion to hear moot cases)
issues: What is the appellate standard of review applicable to a first-instance judge's mootness determination and exercise of discretion whether to hear a moot case
Whether the case remains a live controversy because declaratory relief sought would support a separate damages claim
Whether the 'evading review' branch of the mootness doctrine applies to repeatedly re-issued short-duration emergency travel orders
Whether a suspended (not repealed) measure that could be reimposed defeats a mootness finding
Whether public importance of the issues and resources already expended by the parties should weigh in favour of hearing a moot case
Whether the Minister's temporary travel orders were intra vires the enabling federal aviation/rail/public health legislation
Whether the travel restriction orders infringed Charter rights and, if so, were justified under s.1
What deference an appellate court owes to a lower court's discretionary decision not to exercise its residual discretion to hear a moot appeal
key_facts: Temporary federal orders barred unvaccinated persons from domestic flights and passenger trains during a public-health emergency
Orders were repeatedly re-issued over approximately eight months
Applicants included a former elected official
Substantial evidentiary record built pre-hearing: expert reports, many affidavits, weeks of cross-examinations
Government rescinded the measures and moved to strike/dismiss the applications as moot before the hearing
Applications judge found the matter moot and declined to exercise discretion to hear it regardless
Applicants argue live controversy persists to support future damages claims, that measures were only suspended and could be reimposed, and that such short-duration measures will evade review
Applicants also argue public importance and resources invested favour hearing the case
Matter is now on appeal from the mootness/discretion ruling
causes_of_action: Application for judicial review of ministerial orders as ultra vires enabling statute
Charter challenge to travel restriction orders (ss. 2, 6, 7, 15 and s.1 justification)
Motion to strike/dismiss application for review as moot
candidate_statutes: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms
